sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for slide drawing
sections.what: Brings in the type for content that can appear as text, the citation helpers and the shared slide data types. It does not show anything on screen.
sections.why: Lets the slide layouts use the same citations and data shapes as the rest of the deck.

sections.name: SCORE_CLASS, SCORE_LABEL
sections.title: Score colours and labels
sections.what: Gives each score (strength, mixed, challenge, neutral, no evidence) a colour and a readable label. Challenge is shown in red as a risk label.
sections.why: Keeps scores the same colour and wording across every slide.
sections.watch_out: The label says Challenge while the score name is risk. A reader comparing the code to the data must remember this mapping.

sections.name: OUTCOME_CLASS, MARK, pg
sections.title: Outcome colours, verification marks and page labels
sections.what: Gives each project outcome a colour, a mark for each verification status, and a page number label when a slide spans several pages.
sections.why: Makes outcomes and source checks easy to read at a glance.
sections.watch_out: A verification status not listed here shows a dot instead of a mark, which hides its real meaning.

sections.name: Frame, H, Gap
sections.title: Slide frame, headings and gap note
sections.what: The common frame gives every content slide a red top bar, a section label, a title, a body area and a footer with the slide number. The heading and gap helpers draw bold red sub-headings and an italic note saying what evidence is missing.
sections.why: Keeps the look consistent and makes missing evidence visible to the reader.
sections.watch_out: Long titles are cut to two lines, so very long titles may lose their end.

sections.name: Table
sections.title: Table helper
sections.what: Draws a table with a dark header row, given column widths and rows of content.
sections.why: Many slides use tables, and this keeps them looking the same.
sections.watch_out: Column widths are fixed percentages, so too many columns can crowd the text.

sections.name: Facts
sections.title: Facts list
sections.what: Lists facts with a verification mark, the fact text, its citation and the publisher where known.
sections.why: Lets readers check each fact against its source.
sections.watch_out: An unknown verification status shows a dot, which may be mistaken for a complete check.

sections.name: DeckSlideView (part 1)
sections.title: Cover, summary and first slide layouts
sections.what: Draws the cover with a title, subtitle and date, the executive summary with bullets, evidence gaps and headline numbers, the agenda with a highlighted active item, the section divider, and the recipe overview with one column per pillar.
sections.why: These slides set the story and the structure of the deck.
sections.watch_out: The agenda needs the active value to be a position in the list, so a wrong value highlights the wrong item.

sections.name: DeckSlideView (part 2)
sections.title: Pillar and sub-driver layouts
sections.what: Draws the pillar detail slide with sub-drivers, methodology grounding, practices that worked, implications and a balance count of strengths, mixed and challenges, plus a discrimination note. Also draws the sub-driver profile with good examples, gaps and cautionary tales.
sections.why: These slides hold the detailed reasoning behind each pillar and sub-driver.
sections.watch_out: The discrimination note shows an insufficient sample message when there are too few projects, so a short sample is labelled rather than hidden.

sections.name: DeckSlideView (part 3)
sections.title: Rubric, universe and matrix layouts
sections.what: Draws the rubric table showing what success, mixed and challenge look like for each pillar. Draws the universe slide with outcome counts and grouped project names. Draws the project by pillar matrix with coloured scores.
sections.why: These slides let readers see the scoring rules, the full project list, and how each project scored.
sections.watch_out: The matrix colours cells by score and hides not-applicable cells as blank, so a missing score looks empty rather than marked.

sections.name: DeckSlideView (part 4)
sections.title: Synthesis, glossary and performance layouts
sections.what: Draws the synthesis grid of pillars against outcomes with cited patterns or a no-pattern note. Draws the glossary pages from table rows. Draws a scatter chart of cost overrun against schedule delay, with approximate points marked and a list of projects left off the chart with reasons.
sections.why: These slides summarise patterns, define terms and show the main cost and time picture.
sections.watch_out: The chart scale always includes at least 50 percent cost and 12 months delay. The positions are calculated from the data, so one extreme project can compress the rest.

sections.name: DeckSlideView (part 5)
sections.title: Programme, learning, method, verification and abbreviations layouts
sections.what: Draws the programme table by country with outcome counts and score counts per pillar, the learning slide with cited points and supporting facts, the method slide with thesis, qualifications and a source table, the verification slide with statistics and held-back reasons, and the abbreviations list.
sections.why: These slides explain the scope, the method and the checks behind the deck.
sections.watch_out: The verification slide shows held-back counts as numbers from the data, so any change in the wording of a reason changes what the reader sees.

sections.name: DeckSlideView (part 6)
sections.title: Case layouts and closing slide
sections.what: Draws each case summary with outcome, identity details, headline, takeaways and perspectives. Draws the case factbase grouped by pillar. Draws the closing slide with title and note. Any slide kind not listed falls through and draws nothing.
sections.why: These slides give the per-project story and close the deck.
sections.watch_out: Any new slide kind that is not added to the switch will draw nothing, so the slide appears empty.

summary: This file draws each slide of the lessons deck in the browser on a fixed-size canvas, so the on-screen deck matches the downloaded deck slide for slide.
purpose: Lets users read every slide of the recipe-v3 deck inside the app, with the same content and layout as the file download.
why: The header states that the file draws the same deck data as the file export so the two stay matched. Reason for the fixed size is not fully stated, though a 1280 by 720 canvas is a common slide shape.
how: It defines colours and labels for scores and outcomes, a shared frame with a section title and footer, small helper pieces for headings, tables, evidence gaps and factbase lists. Then one large switch chooses the layout for each slide kind, such as cover, executive summary, pillar detail, rubric, scatter chart, matrix, glossary, closing and others.
inputs: One slide of deck data, its position number and the total number of slides.
outputs: The drawn slide on screen, with citations, tables, charts and footers.
risks: Each slide kind has its own layout, so a new kind added to the data but not to the switch will draw nothing. Fixed sizes may cut off long text, since overflow is hidden. Charts use positions computed from the data, so one extreme value can squash the others.
debug: If a slide is blank, check its kind name against the switch cases. If text is cut off, check its length and the hidden overflow. If a chart looks wrong, check the cost and delay values and the maximum values used for scale.
